description: Find businesses that take walk-ins, by US city, near a point, by the business's name or by ZIP code, with how long the wait is right now. Open places come first, shortest wait first. Use it when someone wants to go now without an appointment: a walk-in visit near them, who has the shortest wait, who is taking walk-ins today, how long the line is, or to check in online before they go. It covers live walk-in lines, not reviews or ratings, and not restaurant tables. Optionally narrow to one kind of business with `trade`: barbershops (barbershop), hair-salons (hair salon), nail-salons (nail salon), brow-and-lash (brow and lash studio), massage-and-spas (massage studio or spa), tattoo-shops (tattoo shop), pet-groomers (pet groomer), vet-clinics (vet clinic), chiropractors (walk-in chiropractor), tax-preparers (tax preparation office), auto-repair (auto repair shop), car-washes (car wash), phone-repair (phone repair shop). Returns at most 10 places, each with its slug, city, wait and a link to join the line. Pass `name` (part of a business or location name, any case) to look up a specific place without knowing its city, e.g. "how long is the wait at Fade Factor on Gum Branch"; then city and state are optional and only narrow the match. For "near me" questions, pass `latitude` and `longitude` (the person's own, or the assistant's knowledge of a place they named) to find places within `radiusMiles` (1 to 50, default 10), or pass city and state with `radiusMiles` to search around that town (only a town with listed places has a known center; for any other town give its latitude and longitude); each place then has `miles`, and open places come first, then nearest. Pass `zip` (5 digits) to find places whose address is in that exact ZIP code only; it doesn't search nearby ZIPs, so for "near" use a radius search around the town instead. Give city and state, or latitude and longitude, or name, or zip. Each place has `openNow` (its line takes check-ins now), `hoursToday` and `outsidePostedHours`: true means the business opened its line early or kept it open late, which is its choice, so say the line is taking check-ins outside its posted hours rather than calling it a mistake. `waitMinutes` is null when the place doesn't work out minutes: give `peopleWaiting` as a count then, never turn it into minutes. `updatedAt` is when the waits were read (UTC). Pass `service` (a few words, e.g. "oil change", "gel manicure", "beard trim") with any of those to keep only places that publicly list a service with those words in its name; each place then has `service` (`id`, `name`, `price`, `minutes`) for its best match. `price` is exactly as the place shows it ("$30", "from $45", empty when the place hides it): compare it across places for "cheapest" questions, and say when a place doesn't show a price. `minutes` is only there when the place shows lengths. The service `id` works with available_times, join_link and booking_link. It checks the first 30 places in the usual order, so narrow by city, radius or trade for a wider search. Start here when you don't have a place's slug yet; use get_place for one place's full details. If nothing is listed in that city or radius (or for that trade), it says so and names up to 3 nearest cities that do have places (with `miles` when known) instead of returning places; if no place has a matching service, it says so.

city.description: City name, e.g. Austin. Required with state unless name or zip is given

latitude.description: Optional latitude in degrees (-90 to 90) to search near; needs longitude; not with name or zip

longitude.description: Optional longitude in degrees (-180 to 180) to search near; needs latitude. US longitudes are negative (west), e.g. -97.74 for Austin

name.description: Optional part of a business or location name to look up, e.g. Fade Factor

radiusMiles.description: Optional search radius in miles, 1 to 50 (default 10); with latitude and longitude, or with city and state

service.description: Optional service to look for, a few words, e.g. oil change; works with every other option

state.description: Two-letter US state code, e.g. TX. Required with city

trade.description: Optional kind of business, one of the slugs listed in the tool description

zip.description: Optional 5-digit US ZIP code, e.g. 80302; matches the ZIP on places' addresses

name: find_walk_in_places
title: Find walk-in places
